title: Synthesis and electrochemical properties of a bio-based  N -propyl-tris(3-lauroylamidopropyl) ammonium iodide salt for electrochemical applications
content: This research demonstrates a purification method for a bio-based N-propyl-tris(3-lauroylamidopropyl) ammonium iodide (TASI) salt synthesized from lauric acid via amidation and quaternization. Amidation was verified by FTIR spectroscopy, with characteristic N–H stretching (3282 cm−1), C═  O stretching (1633 cm−1), and N–H bending (1641 cm−1). The subsequent Menshutkin reaction with iodopropane quaternized the nitrogen core. Liquid–liquid extraction optimized fatty amidoalkyl amine (FA) separation, achieving a 43% increase in the relative ion abundance of tri-substituted TAS, as confirmed by LC-ToF-MS (m/z 777). Physicochemical analysis revealed that at 50 °C, 0.10 M TAS exhibited a reduced viscosity of 0.67 mPa s and an increased conductivity of 0.22 × 10−3 S cm−1. While the 0.1 M concentration generated the peak current (69.8 µA), the 0.025 M concentration yielded the highest diffusion coefficient (1.01 × 10−10 cm2 s−1). This discrepancy is attributed to the formation of bulky iodine–iodide complexes at higher concentrations. These larger entities increase migratory resistance, thereby hindering ionic mobility and reducing the diffusion coefficient compared to those of free iodide ions.
